sources.outlet: City AM (Maria Ward-Brennan), citing The Times
sources.quote: The weekly figures for incorporations dropped from 18,199 in the week before the rules came into effect to fewer than 13,000 in each of the five weeks leading up to Christmas.
sources.searcher_note: Same finding at weekly grain: registrations fell about 30% after ID checks began. Numbers look UK-wide, not England and Wales. No single-day 18 Nov figure.

sources.quote: Weekly incorporations have fallen by around 30 per cent since November, when legislation came into force requiring all new company directors and people with significant control to verify their identity.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest coverage found. Same weekly drop and same 18,199 to under-13,000 figures; source not named on the page (City AM credits The Times).

sources.quote: There were 184,888 incorporations in the UK during October to December 2025. This is a decrease of 31,094 (14.40%) compared with July to September 2025
sources.searcher_note: Quarterly UK figure, down 14.4% on the quarter but up 2.0% on a year earlier. Notes ID verification began 18 Nov 2025 but does not blame the drop on it. No daily or weekly numbers.

sources.quote: There were 204,612 incorporations in the UK during January to March 2026. This is an increase of 19,724 (10.67%) compared with October to December 2025, and a decrease of 6,500 (3.08%) compared with the same period in 2025.
sources.searcher_note: Q1 2026 rebounded on the quarter but ran 3.1% BELOW Q1 2025. The lead says January 2026 ran 4-7% above January 2025. That is a different window (one month vs a quarter), and the national figures are UK-wide.

sources.outlet: SME Magazine (Dan Martin), reporting NatWest and Beauhurst
sources.quote: However, the 402,000 companies incorporated during that period was a 5.7% decrease on the first half of 2025 and a second consecutive half-year decline.
sources.searcher_note: Recent: H1 2026 incorporations down 5.7% year on year; the report blames identity verification more than fees. Cuts against the lead's caveat that the dip did not last.

sources.quote: 461,765 new companies were incorporated between January and July 2026.
sources.searcher_note: Recent and opposite to NatWest/Beauhurst: says Jan-Jul 2026 formations were up 6.9% on the same period of 2025. Does not mention the late-2025 dip.

notes: The weekly drop after 18 Nov 2025 (about 30%, 18,199 to under 13,000 a week, UK-wide) was reported in late December 2025 by City AM, Business Matters and The Times (the Times original was not found). That matches the lead's 29% five-week drop in direction and roughly in size, but the lead uses England and Wales figures (15,790 vs 11,158 a week). No source found gives the single-day figure (847 on Tue 18 Nov vs 3,156 the Tuesday before, -73%), the 16,000-fewer estimate, or the 10,338 of 64,456 company numbers (16%) that match no company. Companies House's own quarterly releases note the ID verification date but do not tie the Q4 2025 fall to it. Its 'Companies register activities 2025-26' release (2026-06-25) says nothing about an ID-verification effect. 2026 sources disagree on whether the dip lasted. NatWest/Beauhurst: H1 2026 -5.7% year on year. Official Q1 2026: -3.1% year on year. Icon Offices: Jan-Jul 2026 +6.9%. House of Commons Library briefing CBP-10015 returned 403 and was not read.
